source.title: OrtSAE: Orthogonal Sparse Autoencoders Uncover Atomic Features
source.authors: Anton Korznikov; Andrey V. Galichin; Alexey Dontsov; Oleg Y. Rogov; Elena Tutubalina; I. Oseledets

record.tranche_reason: The study trains and evaluates SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B, extending indirect evidence about sparse dictionary features to LLM activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses superposition, but does not test its toy-model claims about sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, capacity allocation among neurons, or feature dimensionality. Rows cover the study's own SAE feature analyses and downstream evaluations. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: A methods paper. It trains a new SAE variant (OrtSAE) on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B and reports how it compares with ReLU, BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs on reconstruction, absorption, composition, interpretability and SAEBench tasks. Superposition and SAE recovery of features are assumed as the motivation. No result tests whether features are superposed, whether SAEs recover the model's features (V4), or whether dictionary features are canonical (V5). The comparisons rank dictionary-learning methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that an orthogonality penalty on SAE decoder features reduces absorption and composition, gives 9% more distinct features and +6% SCR, keeps reconstruction comparable, and adds little compute. Their remark that this offers 'fresh perspectives on the superposition hypothesis' is a closing assertion, not a tested result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a chunk-wise orthogonality penalty during SAE training and evaluates learned dictionaries on LLM activations; it does not use the original toy-model setup or its feature-geometry intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results across sparsity levels and layers; in chunk-count experiments, cosine similarity and absorption/composition rise somewhat as chunk count increases. It also varies whether the orthogonality loss is computed every training step or every fifth step.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B (layer 20, L0=70) show nonzero absorption (BatchTopK 0.220 and 0.148; ReLU 0.371 and 0.490) and MetaSAE composition (about 0.41–0.53). Different SAE training objectives yield substantially different dictionaries: 9% of OrtSAE features have no BatchTopK counterpart above cosine 0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary features depend on the training objective and contain absorbed or composite latents, a benchmark-level indication against V5-style canonicity, though the study does not test this directly.

record.code_released: not stated (the authors say code will be released anonymously as supplementary material and made public upon acceptance)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported comparisons. Several figures are described without numerical values in the text. The feature-recovery evidence is indirect: interpretability uses GPT-4o-mini as judge, and composition, absorption, and qualitative decompositions do not compare SAE features with a ground-truth feature set. Additional model/layer experiments are limited to layer 20 and L0=70.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results were deliberately omitted. Core reconstruction metrics and LogLoss were not included because they assess activation reconstruction or predictive preservation rather than whether SAE dictionaries recover the features named by V4. The 9% unique-feature result is recorded under fits_no_version because it does not measure feature recovery.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no geometry analysis.
No test of capacity allocation or feature importance.
No test of what causes polysemantic neurons.
Assumes SAEs recover sparse features; does not test whether LLM features are distributed or recoverable, only ranks SAE variants.
Absorption and composition are used as benchmarks to improve on, not as a test of whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T3' with V4 supports and limits_scope labels is overreach. Every row compares SAE methods, so the study is reclassified as T4 and the version links are removed. No uncertainty estimates are given. Qualitative examples were selected by approximation cosine similarity above 0.95.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-versus-dimension sweep, or sparsity-dependent transition and regular-geometry test.
The study does not test whether feature importance or capacity pressure determines which features receive dedicated dimensions versus sharing.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than superposition.

Tests SAE-derived features in selected layers of Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B, including interpretability and concept-probing measures; it does not establish recovery of a ground-truth feature set or test whether features are distributed across neurons.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. Feature uniqueness and interpretability results do not establish those properties.
The study computes cosine similarity between decoder vectors but does not test whether underlying model features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12 SAE feature evaluations, including concept probing and qualitative decomposition
reader_labels.reason: The study reports concept-probe accuracy comparable to other SAE methods and gives examples of SAE latents separating concepts; these are indirect indicators of recoverable features (G12-probe, G12-queen, G12-climate, G12-jaw, G12-module).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested SAE feature evaluations on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B
reader_labels.reason: Evidence is indirect, varies by metric and comparator, and does not verify recovery against ground-truth model features; OrtSAE absorption rates also remain higher than Matryoshka SAE in the reported layer-20 tables (G20-ort-abs, L20-ort-abs).
